SGP: Norms and Standards

The first analysis associated with student growth percentiles
is to establish growth norms (usually for the state) in each
subject and grade.
Norms are excellent for describing the distribution of
performance but are not sufficient alone to distinguish
adequate from inadequate.
Standards are required to judge the adequacy of growth.
Student growth projections/percentile growth trajectories are
used to allow states to make adequacy judgments regarding
growth [Betebenner, 2009].

SGP: Growth to Standard

Judging adequacy requires stakeholders to decide “adequate
for what?”.
Specifically, growth is usually judged in terms of its adequacy
to helps students reach/maintain desired levels of
achievement.
The Growth Model Pilot Program was set up by the USDOE to
allow states to use growth for AYP with students being
expected to be on track (i.e., demonstrating growth sufficient)
to reach/maintain proficient status.
Colorado successfully applied as part of the growth model
pilot program to use SGP growth-to-standard analyses.

SGP: Percentile Growth Trajectories

The usual adequacy criteria are for students to reach/maintain
(i.e., catch-up/keep-up to) proficient status within 3 years or by
the end of testing.
Note that given a students initial starting place, a destination,
and a time frame, we are have a situation involving
distance = ratextime.
Using the results from the SGP analyses, percentile
trajectories are estimated for each student indicating what
level of percentile growth is necessary for each student to
reach their desired target in the established time-frame.

Going from Student Target to Group Targets

There are many ways to incorporate student level targets into
accountability discussions
The Colorado GMPP Application tabulated percentages of
students making adequate growth (with little impact on AYP
discussions).
Another approach is to take the median SGP and compare it
to the median target SGP.
Colorado has used the median SGP and median target SGP
for their district and school performance frameworks.
New York is exploring other ways to blend norm and criterion
referenced growth to satisfy AYP determinations.
